summary: Temporary elevation sessions still permit user impersonation after expiry due to session cache mismatch
description:
Issue summary: A user who received temporary 'oncall-sudo' elevation via JIT access retained the ability to impersonate other users (impersonation API succeeded) for up to ~7 minutes after the elevation TTL expired. This appears to be caused by a mismatch between Okta session invalidation and the in-memory session cache on the auth-proxy nodes.

Impact: Elevated privileges persisted beyond TTL for a small subset of ephemeral sessions. Affects recent oncall rotations in prod-us-west. Potential security exposure: unauthorized access using impersonation endpoints until cache eviction. No public customer data exfiltrated known; internal dashboards impacted.

Timeline:
- 2026-02-10 08:12 PST: Oncall reported they could still impersonate after elevation was auto-revoked by JIT service.
- 2026-02-10 08:18 PST: Support triaged and escalated to SRE.
- 2026-02-10 09:05 PST: SRE observed auth-proxy cache retention beyond TTL on two nodes.
- 2026-02-10 10:40 PST: Patch branch created to add immediate cache invalidation on JIT-revoke webhooks.

Environment: production (us-west), auth-proxy fleet behind ALB, session-store is Redis (cache shards A/B), Okta session invalidation via SCIM/Webhooks.

Steps to reproduce (dev-forward):
1. Create test user and request JIT elevation (oncall-sudo) with TTL 5m.
2. Use impersonation endpoint to act as another test user - confirm success while elevated.
3. Wait until TTL expires according to JIT service and Okta shows elevation revoked.
4. Immediately hit impersonation endpoint from same auth-proxy node - observe success for ~5-8 minutes intermittently.

Observed: Auth-proxy consults local in-memory session cache which is asynchronously refreshed from Redis. When JIT service revokes a session it sends a webhook that clears Redis, but some auth-proxy nodes only refresh on cache expiration rather than on webhook, leaving stale elevated sessions active.

Expected: Impersonation should fail immediately after revocation and TTL expiry.

Logs/Artifacts:
- auth-proxy logs (node-ap-03): "session_lookup: user=alice, elevation=oncall-sudo=true, ttl=0s, cache_hit=true" (2026-02-10T08:13:02Z)
- Redis key absent after webhook processed (confirmed at 2026-02-10T08:13:20Z)
- ALB request ids and timestamps attached in the S3 bundle "s3://redwood-support/prod-us-west/INT-563210/log-bundle-20260210.tar.gz"

Mitigation applied: Temporary mitigation rolled out 2026-02-10 11:05 PST: forced eviction script executed across all auth-proxy nodes to clear in-memory caches; HTTP 200 responses from impersonation endpoint dropped to expected denies.

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis: race between webhook processing and local cache refresh; in-memory cache TTL set to 10m on some older auth-proxy nodes.
- Confirmed: two auth-proxy instances (ap-02, ap-03) running legacy binary with cache-sync behavior that only polls Redis every 10m.
- Reproducible in staging after flipping poll interval to 10m.

Next steps:
1) Code change to cause JIT revoke webhook to send a targeted SSE/GRPC invalidation message to auth-proxy fleet (PR reference below).
2) Short-term config change: reduce poll interval to 30s and roll legacy instances.
3) Audit of other cached permissions paths for similar race conditions.
4) Postmortem and communication to security and oncall teams.

Suggested workaround: If immediate denial is required, run the provided eviction script (ops/scripts/evict-auth-cache.sh) targeting auth-proxy nodes via the maintenance API.

Resolution: In Progress (code patch pending review and rollout).

resolution_notes: Forced eviction completed 2026-02-10 11:05 PST; immediate impact mitigated. Patch for targeted invalidation created and under review. Full roll-out scheduled after code review and canary on 2026-02-12.
canary_plan: Roll out auth-proxy invalidation patch to canary group (ap-canary) -> monitor impersonation failure rates and 500s for 30m -> proceed to full fleet.
